name: TX-37
label: Safe D

key_factors: Casar's large fundraising and cash advantage
Prediction markets price near-certain Democratic win
model.rationale: The D+30 district fundamentals and Casar's roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge over Peña, who has under $1,000 on hand, point to a decisive Democratic win, and Polymarket prices a Democratic victory at about 97%. No polls or expert ratings contradict the safe-D picture.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unusually weak Democratic margin or major outside spending against Casar would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Austin-based TX-37 is one of the most Democratic districts in Texas, with a partisan lean of D+30, and incumbent Greg Casar is running for renomination and reelection. He has raised about $1.17 million and holds nearly $600,000 in cash, while Republican Lauren Peña has raised under $120,000 and reports only $770 on hand. No outside groups are spending against Casar.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and campaign resources. Prediction markets put Democratic odds around 97 percent. The combination of an overwhelming partisan lean, a well-funded incumbent, and a cash-starved challenger makes this a Safe Democratic seat with a high degree of confidence.
